_meta.scope: Project-level, single source of truth for character x form -> TTS casting. All synthesis (voiceprint samples now; dialogue-tts-library / p7-dub later, when those output settings are on) must read this table before calling genmedia tts; missing entry = register here first.
_meta.mode_note: seed-audio-1.0 is the description-custom voice model (WORKFLOW.md / SOUL.md 09-audio/voice-generation duty 1): no tts_voice is selected from a library. Each entry's voice_desc is the acoustic description (gender + pitch + timbre + accent, taken verbatim from the character's voice.json, per genmedia.py:_seedaudio_char_desc) that genmedia assembles and that the model echoed back in its synthesis log (modules/genmedia.py stderr 'desc=' line) when the sample below was produced. --voice must never be passed in this mode (SOUL.md red line: a stale speaker/voice-id string would be ignored by the model and silently misleads future callers).
_meta.sample_command: python3 modules/genmedia.py tts --character <CHAR-id> [--variant <variant>] --text "<calm neutral line>" --output assets/audio/voice/refs/<CHAR-id>[_<variant>]_voiceprint.mp3 --project alices
_meta.speed_field_note: speed is a numeric multiplier (1.0 = project default output.dialogue_tts_speed). All entries below use the project default; genmedia was not called with --speed for any of these samples.
_meta.reference_anchor_note: genmedia auto-anchors a variant's synthesis on the character's already-frozen base-form sample when one exists on disk at call time (modules/genmedia.py:_seedaudio_ref), passed to the model as @Audio 1 so the variant is recognisably the same voice aged/altered per its own description. Base forms have no prior sample to anchor on ('pure description'). This project only has one such case: CHAR-alice age02 anchors on CHAR-alice's base sample (synthesised first, in that order, for exactly this reason).
_meta.duration_check: machine gate = sample duration in [3,5]s (SOUL.md quality standard; anything over 5s risks tripping the Ark reference_audio 15.2s total cap once 2-3 samples are stacked as reference_audio in a group). Measured post-hoc via ffprobe on the actual output files (genmedia's own console log reports the provider's 'original_duration', which is consistently ~0.05-0.3s lower than the saved-file duration - ffprobe on the saved file is the value graded against the gate).
_meta.duration_check_result: 12/39 forms measured inside [3,5]s; 27/39 measured over 5s (range 5.35-8.66s) even though every text line was sized to the character's own voice.json speed_wpm for a ~4s target. Cause: seed-audio-1.0 does not track the requested character speaking-rate at all when no --speed override is sent - actual per-character delivery pace (pauses, breath, drawl implied by the acoustic description) varied far more than speed_wpm predicts, so word-count calibration alone cannot hit the window reliably for this model. Per project auto-retry-count=0 (Web client Agent settings), no automatic re-synthesis was attempted for the 27 over-length forms: they are kept as produced and flagged failed below (see each entry's duration_check) for orchestrator/user disposition (candidates: shorten each flagged line and resynthesise as an explicit follow-up work order, or pass a small --speed>1.0 nudge; both are new decisions, not retries of this task). Voiceprint samples are reference_audio timbre anchors only - see assets/audio/voice/refs/manifest.json _meta.duration_gate_status for the full failing-id list and downstream handling note.
_meta.collision_review: Not a shared-voice-id collision risk in this mode (each character's voice_desc is independently authored text, not a pooled speaker id), so graded per SOUL.md's seed-audio amendment: same-scene speakers must not read as timbre/pitch look-alikes. Spot-checked the highest-contact scenes (tea party: hatter/march-hare/dormouse; croquet garden: gardener-two/five/seven; court: king-of-hearts/queen-of-hearts/knave-of-hearts; kitchen: duchess/cook; seaside: old-crab/young-crab; footmen: fish-footman/frog-footman) - all distinct on both pitch register and timbre adjective. No collision_waivers needed. Full pairwise (741-combination) semantic-similarity diff of all 39 descriptions was not run; each was independently authored per-character by 03-characters/voiceprint (task p3-voice-vb1) with source-cited distinguishing detail, which is the review basis here.
_meta.open_tickets_checked: qa/defects/DEF-p3-char-index-902.json (executioner: no axe/block/execution device) is a prop/costume constraint, not a voice one - the neutral sample line for CHAR-executioner makes no reference to any execution device, no action needed from this table. qa/defects/DEF-p3-char-index-903.json (ch006 lullaby CHORUS = Duchess+cook+baby) is a dialogue-attribution ticket for 01-story/screenplay; CHAR-duchess and CHAR-cook are already individually cast below (their own samples cover those chorus lines per the ticket's own requested_action - 'cast ... from the Duchess/cook/baby voice models, not a crowd-ensemble group voice'); CHAR-duchess-baby has no voice.json (03-characters/voiceprint did not card it - a baby has no describable adult-speech timbre) so no casting entry is created for it here; nothing further required of this task.
